transcript:
Header: 2026-12-01 16:00 UTC | Duration approx 48 minutes | Redwood: Aisha Khan, Ben Turner | BlueWave: Marta Ruiz, Daniel Cho, Samir Patel

Summary: Quick scoping call to align on benchmark plan and harness integration for the POC. Focus: success criteria, workload sizing, streaming vs non-streaming, customer scripts, load testing timeline and responsibilities.

00:00 Speaker 1 (Aisha): Hey everyone thanks for joining, we wanted to run through the benchmark plan for the POC and make sure the harness integration will work with your existing scripts and infra.
00:18 Marta Ruiz: Thanks Aisha, yeah we've been looking at Redwood's docs, and the thing for us is verifying latency tail and token cost per query for our named-entity extraction pipelines. Success criteria are realtime <= 120ms p95 for short queries and cost under our threshold.
00:45 Ben Turner: Right, so two axes: latency (p50/p95/p99) and cost per 1k tokens. Also quality regressions — we'll want a small eval set to track accuracy. We'll propose a mixed load: a steady-state non-streaming traffic and a streaming workload for session-based flows.
01:12 Daniel Cho: Just to clarify are you recommending streaming mode only for chat-like flows? Our infra currently has a websocket layer for streaming but most batch jobs are non-streaming.
01:28 Ben Turner: Exactly. Streaming is beneficial for interactive sessions, it reduces perceived latency but it's more sensitive to connection churn. For throughput and cost comparisons we should run both.
01:45 Samir Patel: Our main scripts are in Python, we call your hosted REST now for dev. For the POC we can adapt one of our flask-based streaming clients. We'll also share a non-streaming batch runner.
02:05 Aisha Khan: Great. On harness integration: Ben will share the GitHub repo with the Redwood benchmark harness. It supports plugging in customer scripts — we usually ask for a wrapper that accepts a JSON request and returns token counts and timings.
02:32 Ben Turner: I can walk through the connector pattern: we expect a small adapter (10-20 lines) that maps your request format to the harness. We'll also provide an example streaming client and a non-streaming runner.
03:00 Marta Ruiz: For success criteria, beyond p95 latency and cost, we need throughput targets — peak 200 rps for non-streaming and concurrent 80 streaming sessions during peak. Also, accuracy drop must be <2% compared to our baseline model.
03:25 Ben Turner: Noted. We'll parameterize the harness to run a mix: 70% short queries (<=64 tokens), 25% medium (65-256), 5% long (>256). We can vary batch sizes and quantization profiles to see cost/latency tradeoffs.
03:48 Daniel Cho: Network — we need to decide whether we'll run against Redwood hosted API or Redwood Private (VPC). If private, we'll need VPC peering and we may do on-prem later. For now we prefer hosted to reduce setup time unless security blocks it.
04:10 Aisha Khan: Understood. We'll send our security package and SOC 2 docs; if that's acceptable you can start with hosted. If not, we'll scope private deployment and timelines.
04:30 Marta Ruiz: Also curious about KV cache/prefix caching — many of our requests have repeated prefixes. Can you include caching in the benchmark?
04:45 Ben Turner: Yes we can instrument the harness to enable prefix/KV caching and measure cache hit rate and tail latency. We'll run scenarios with cache cold and warmed.
05:05 Samir Patel: For load testing, do you run the spike tests or just steady-state? We want both — a 10x spike test to ensure graceful degradation and fallback to smaller model variants.
05:24 Ben Turner: We'll run both steady-state and spike. For graceful degradation we'll test routing policies: fallback to smaller model or lower quantized profile. We'll capture error rates and time-to-recover.
05:40 Marta Ruiz: Timeline — we want results within two weeks of starting the harness tests. Can you commit to that?
05:50 Aisha Khan: Yes, if we get the sample scripts and dataset by Dec 2, Ben's team can run tests and deliver an initial report by Dec 15. That's about a two-week turnaround.
06:06 Daniel Cho: Who owns the run scheduling? We can run from our infra or Redwood can kick off from your harness.
06:15 Ben Turner: We prefer to run the harness centrally (Redwood CI) with your scripts mounted or fetched from your repo. Alternatively, we can provide a runner you execute on your side and push logs. Both okay; left to customer preference.
06:35 Marta Ruiz: We'll likely have you run it first to reduce infra setup, then replicate on our side.
06:44 Aisha Khan: Ok next steps: I'll share pricing and the SOW draft. Ben will send the harness link and an adapter example. Marta/Samir to share scripts and datasets. Daniel to confirm network preference.
07:00 Samir Patel: Quick question: token counting — our scripts currently estimate tokens via heuristics. Will the harness give exact token counts?
07:10 Ben Turner: The harness will instrument tokenizers (we support common variants) and report token counts per request plus downstream decode tokens. That will feed into cost modeling.
07:25 Marta Ruiz: Any gotchas for streaming measurement? We need consistent timestamping of first byte and final token delivered.
07:35 Ben Turner: We capture send time, first-byte (stream start), and completion time on the client side; we also correlate server-side generate timestamps. There may be small clock skew — we recommend using the harness metrics primarily for comparative analysis rather than absolute single-digit ms claims.
07:58 Daniel Cho: Regarding credentials: for hosted we'll need API keys; for private we'll need service account and VPC details. We'll prepare whichever is needed.
08:10 Aisha Khan: I'll include a checklist in the email.
08:16 Marta Ruiz: OK, any other questions?
08:20 Samir Patel: One more — we'd like to test quantized model variants (8-bit) to compare cost vs quality. Is that supported in the harness?
08:28 Ben Turner: Yes, we can run quantization profiles and report quality regression metrics on your eval set. We'll include the quantized vs float baselines in the report.
08:45 Aisha Khan: Thanks all. Recap and owners: Aisha send pricing/SOW; Ben share harness and runbook; BlueWave (Marta/Samir) share scripts/datasets; Daniel confirm network/credential preference. We'll schedule the first run for week of Dec 6.
09:05 Marta Ruiz: Sounds good, thanks everyone.
09:10 Meeting end.

Notes: Transcript contains occasional small disfluencies and filler; some technical terms may be transcribed imperfectly (e.g., KV cache as K-V cache). Links referenced: Redwood benchmark harness repo (to be shared by Ben), security package (to be emailed by Aisha).
